newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW - Equitable of Iowa deal aimed at sales.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Equitable of Iowa deal aimed at sales.

text.p: Equitable of Iowa Cos Inc said its proposed purchase by Dutch financial company ING Groep NV for $2.6 billion is intended to boost revenue growth and was not designed to enhance profits through cost cutting.

"We believe this transaction is designed to create top-line sales opportunity...," Fred Hubbell, chairman of Equitable, said in a telephone interview. "The transaction is not based on cutting expenses to improve profits."
ING agreed to buy Equitable for $2.2 billion, or $68 a share, and to assume $400 million in Equitable debt.
After the merger, Equitable will expand distribution of ING's life insurance products, particularly through a network of bank and brokerage channels, Hubbell said.
In addition, Equitable's portfolio of fixed and variable annuities will bolster ING's product offerings.
"There are significant cross-selling synergies between the two businesses just to begin with," Hubbell said.
Equitable markets fixed and variable annuities and fixed and variable life insurance products through independent and career insurance agents, banks and broker/dealers.
ING is involved in banking, insurance and asset management on a global basis.
ING's proposed purchase of Equitable reflects the consolidation in the insurance industry, a trend that is expected to continue, said Everen Securities analyst C. Gregory Peters.

"Insurance companies are looking for top-line growth. They're looking for strategic growth into new products. They're looking for new distribution channels," said Peters, who follows the insurance industry, but not Equitable in particular.
Other recent acquisitions in the insurance industry include Conseco Inc's purchase of Pioneer Financial Services Inc and SAFECO Corp's purchase of American States Financial.
Hubbell declined to comment on a possible competing bid for Equitable, but said the ING offer is a "very attractive package of values" for shareholders, employees and customers.

However, from the time ING first approached Equitable in late 1996 or early 1997 until the present, other companies have expressed an interest in possibly acquiring Equitable, Hubbell acknowledged. He declined to give details.
"I really can't comment on that," Hubbell said. "Certainly there have been other companies that have expressed an interest during that same period of time."

Hubbell retierated that, prior to agreeing to be acquired by ING, Equitable was not for sale. Beyond final terms, ING's offer was attractive based on the Dutch company's commitment to growth and a similar corporate culture.
"If we were going to find a partner, we wanted to align ourselves" with a strong company, Hubbell said.
